day_shape: 65 items: Iran's Deputy FM Gharibabadi outlines 'two-day plan' via Qatar/Pakistan intermediaries and rules out IAEA access, IDF kills Hamas Rafah Brigade commander Samir Abu Younis, UK-Australia-Canada-Italy joint Gaza statement, Bessent calls Iran's economy in 'fastest collapse', heavy regime messaging cycle.

threads.label: Iran-US indirect diplomacy via Gharibabadi
threads.summary: IRIB carried extensive remarks from Deputy Foreign Minister Gharibabadi saying Iran's negotiating plan has been reduced from seven to two days via Qatari and Pakistani intermediaries, with implementation dependent on US action. Gharibabadi said US responses were 'not operational' and accused Washington of using diplomacy to prepare a fresh attack; Araghchi was reported heading to Muscat for talks.

threads.label: IAEA access and 12-day war litigation
threads.summary: Gharibabadi told IRIB that IAEA access will not be restored while war continues and US obligations go unmet, and criticised Director General Grossi for not condemning strikes on Iranian nuclear facilities. He also said 226 criminal cases were formed over the 12-day war and 386 over the 40-day war, with ICJ and Iran-US Claims Tribunal filings underway.

threads.label: US pressure campaign on Iran economy
threads.summary: Iran International reported Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent describing Iran as undergoing one of the fastest economic collapses in history, with Washington expanding pressure beyond a naval blockade to land supply routes. Jerusalem Post cited US intelligence assessments putting Iran's remaining missile stockpile at 1,500–2,500, over half its pre-war level.

threads.label: Iran domestic strains: fuel, pollution, labour
threads.summary: Iran International reported new petrol restrictions triggering shortages and transport-cost warnings, worsening urban air pollution with reported health complaints, a bus crash killing 12 gas refinery workers in western Iran, and the arrest of five job seekers protesting at a southwestern oil company. A separate piece revisited the 2019 crackdown's failure to end recurring protests.

threads.label: IDF operations in Gaza and Lebanon
threads.summary: The IDF and Shin Bet confirmed killing Samir Abu Younis, commander of Hamas's Rafah Brigade, in an overnight strike in southern Gaza, and said troops dismantled a 35-metre Hezbollah tunnel at Majdal Zoun in southern Lebanon. Jerusalem Post reported a Hamas commander struck at Nasser Hospital suffered head injury and leg amputation, and the UK-Australia-Canada-Italy foreign ministers issued a joint Gaza statement.

threads.label: Yemen-Saudi front and Bab el-Mandeb
threads.summary: Defa Press relayed Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree's claims of 6 ballistic missiles fired at Saudi coalition forces in Lahj, two missiles at Riyadh's King Khalid Airport and financial district, and 75 Saudi airstrikes on Yemen in 24 hours. Jerusalem Post reported Saudi-backed Yemeni forces withdrew from an area overlooking the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, ceding ground to the Houthis.

threads.label: Iran deterrence and martyrdom messaging
threads.summary: Khamenei's office posted on 'the heavy cost of miscalculations' by the US and elegy recitations for 'Iran's martyr', while IRGC-linked Defa Press and IRIB trailed videos of a 'new advanced air defence system' and reported discovery of Orbiter-4 drone wreckage in western highlands. Iran International reported the Telegraph claim that Tony Blair's sister-in-law attended an Iran conference US authorities tied to IRGC intelligence recruitment.
